Long Ago, a Guy Paid $300 (Yes, Hundred) for This 1969 Hemi Road Runner 4-Speed, Now It's $250K
46 photos
Photo: Classic Cars of Sarasota
How much is too much for a museum-grade Hemi Mopar, specifically a 1969 Plymouth Road Runner 4-speed post coupe? Asking $250,000—or $249,500 on the showroom floor—seems to sit on the side of the fence where the grass is not so green, despite the car's own factory F8 Ivy Green Metallic livery. Featured on the Classic Cars of Sarasota list of current offers, this 1-of-1 specimen is testing the market's upper ceiling.
Let’s cut to the chase: this car is for sale, for a cool quarter-million bucks. Not unheard of – particularly not in the rarefied realms of 426 Hemi cars. After all, the recent Mecum Dallas/Fort Worth auction saw a couple of spectacular Plymouths go for over 300k – and none were powered by the Elephant V8 legend. Ask my colleague Ciprian Florea about them – he’s covered each sale in detail.
Granted, all those cars were holy grail rarities in their own right, but this ’69 coupe is no dime-a-dozener, either. And it’s got some history – one that lead me to believe someone is flipping the iconic muscle car big time. Think $70K big.
This exact Mopar has crossed the block several times since January 2018, when it stalled at a high bid of $130,000 at Mecum Kissimmee. Four months later, in May 2018 at Mecum Indy, it hammered for that same $130,000 bid, or $143,000 with fees, before bringing $180,000 on Bring a Trailer in January 2024. Listed for $250,000 since April 2025, it has sat unsold for eighteen months – so far , not a single soul thought it would be a good idea to pay up.
Photo: Classic Cars of Sarasota Between January 2024 and October 2026, this car moved precisely 27 miles, from the 84,700 read recorded nearly three years ago to the 84,727 shown on the odometer now. It doesn’t take a rocket sciences degree to figure out this is a trailer queen, a garage jewel, a piece of showroom art, a car show bauble – you get the idea. And, frankly, I don’t think anyone with a quarter-million bucks in hand would consider buying an old car for the fun of driving the nostalgia off.
Peaking of history and memories: Plymouth introduced the Road Runner for the 1968 model year as a back-to-basics, budget-friendly B-body muscle car aimed at young enthusiasts priced out by luxurious grand tourers like the 440-cubic-inch GTX. Management paid $50,000 to Warner Bros. for the rights to the cartoon bird's name and likeness, plus $10,000 to engineer the signature "beep-beep" horn, targeting 14-second quarter-mile capability for less than $3,000.
The recipe was too simple: pillared coupe body style, 383 big-block, four-on-the-floor. That was about it. unless, of course, someone moneyed up and went for the optional 426 Hemi engine and the also optional 3-speed Torqueflite automatic. That was the short version of how one could configure their Road Runner back in 1968. There were no other engines, no other body styles.
Photo: Classic Cars of Sarasota Plymouth had a change of heart and added the hardtop coupe mid-year in ’68, then introduced the 440 Six-Barrel in 1969, and the convertible.
After moving 44,599 units in its inaugural year, the 1969 Plymouth Road Runner captured the coveted Motor Trend Car of the Year award and set an all-time nameplate production record of 84,420 vehicles. That global tally comprised 33,743 pillared two-door coupes, 48,549 pillarless two-door hardtops, and 2,128 first-year convertibles. Within that grand total, 81,105 cars were built to United States specifications, alongside 3,315 Canadian and export deliveries.
Breaking down those 81,105 domestic units reveals 32,368 coupes, 46,847 hardtops, and 1,890 convertibles. The standard 335-hp, 425-lb-ft 383-cubic-inch V8 powered 78,906 cars, split into 31,397 coupes (18,191 4-speeds and 13,206 3-speed TorqueFlite automatics), 45,629 hardtops (21,278 4-speeds and 24,351 automatics), and 1,880 convertibles (769 4-speeds and 1,111 automatics).
The mid-year 390-hp A12 440-cubic-inch Six-Barrel accounted for 1,412 units, comprising 615 coupes (388 4-speeds, 227 automatics) and 797 hardtops (422 4-speeds, 375 automatics).
Photo: Classic Cars of Sarasota At the top of the hierarchy sat the 426-cubic-inch Hemi V8. Unleashed in 1964 as a race-only engine that dominated NASCAR and NHRA competition, the monstruous powerplant became the 425-hp, 490-lb-ft Street Hemi in 1966 with dual Carter AFB 4-barrel carburetors and 10.25:1 compression. In 1969, only 787 US-spec Road Runners received the E74 Hemi option.
421 hardtops (234 manuals, 187 automatics), 10 convertibles (four 4-speeds, six automatics), and 356 coupes (194 4-speeds and 162 automatics, plus 22 Canadian units).
VIN RM21J9G172560 was scheduled for production on November 21, 1968, at the St. Louis, Missouri plant and delivered on March 17, 1969, by Mark Motors Inc. in Arlington Heights, Illinois. Decoded by Galen Govier on June 11, 2007, it is number 17 of 48 St. Louis-built US-spec Hemi coupes in his Registry, 1 of 24 with the D21 4-speed, 1 of 10 with the A34 Super Track Pak, 1 of 3 in F8 paint, and 1-of-1 with all those combined.
Photo: Classic Cars of Sarasota The original window sticker show a $2,928.00 base price for the RM21 two-door coupe. Factory options added $1,362.35, led by the E74 426-cubic-inch 2x4-barrel Hemi V8 at $813.45 and the A34 Super Track Pak—bundling a 4.10:1 Dana 60 9.75-inch rear axle, 7-blade viscous fan, and 26-inch radiator—at $256.45.
Extras included the A87 Road Runner Decor Group ($81.50), R11 AM radio ($61.55), B41 front disc brakes ($48.70), B51 power brakes ($42.95), D91 Sure-Grip differential ($42.35), and S78 full-horn-ring wheel ($15.40), plus $40.00 destination for a $4,330.35 total. That was downright Hemi GTX territory, or Pontiac GTO Judge Ram Air IV, and inched perilously close to Yenko Super Camaros and Boss 429 Mustangs.
Long before achieving collector status, this Hemi muscle car lived a gritty life on the street and drag strip, with documented history tracing back to 1976. Registered with the National Hemi Owners Association in 1986 and 1990, one of its three early owners included club president Jack Sharkey. During the January 2024 Bring a Trailer auction, a former caretaker who rescued the neglected Mopar in 1983 shared how he found it.
Photo: Classic Cars of Sarasota "I owned that RR between 1983 and 2003. I know history back to 1976. I called it my Army Staff car back then. I have videos and photos going back to car shows and drag racing it. I paid 3,00.00 dollars for it out of the local advertiser. It was mostly in primer, rod bearing loose, 4 flat tires, two frozen rear brake drums all the chrome was in the trunk. I remember the first time I lifted the hood, Boy! I couldn’t get the money out of the pocket fast enough.”
Let’s pause for a second and consider that number: three HUNDRED dollars – legal money of the United States, in other words – for a Hemi Mopar . One that’s gunning for a quarter million today. The $300 from 1983 would equal in purchasing power to about $1,015 today. Again, no rocket scientist is required to do the math.
“I am so happy to see it has lived on and in a good shape. Good luck to the new owner!!" I should say, he looks like luck is not so eager to knock on his door – not in the form of a buyer, anyway. Then again, when someone has $180k to bury invest in a car they move nine miles a year, I don’t think luck is absent from their life.
Photo: Classic Cars of Sarasota Following that 20-year tenure, Mike Paremsky of Michael's Auto Restoration in Winter Haven, Florida, performed a comprehensive rotisserie restoration. The body shell was stripped and acid-dipped—preserving the factory stampings on the radiator core support and trunk lip—before receiving F8 Ivy Green Metallic basecoat/clearcoat paint over an H2X black deluxe vinyl bench-seat interior.
The numbers-matching 426-cubic-inch Hemi, A833 New Process 4-speed manual transmission, N96 Coyote Duster Air Grabber hood, and redline F70x15 tires with Plymouth Division hubcaps look so much better than when the car left the assembly line. Not a metaphor – Ma’ Mopar was famous for drivetrains and suspensions, not so much for fit and finish. (Anyone care to remember the biggest recall in the history of Detroit? Hint: the Road Runner was part of it).
Period magazine road tests demonstrated the potency of a showroom-stock 1969 Hemi Road Runner even when hampered by narrow bias-ply street tires. In 1969, Motor Trend recorded a 0-to-60 mph sprint of 5.1 seconds and a quarter-mile time of 13.56 seconds at 105.38 mph, while Car and Driver achieved 13.54 seconds at 105.14 mph and Super Stock & Drag Illustrated posted 13.32 seconds at 106.5 mph.
Photo: Classic Cars of Sarasota Prepared for the strip with sticky tires and 4.10:1 gears, however, a 4-speed B-body Hemi delivered a far more violent 11-second rush, as a fellow enthusiast recounted on bringatrailer.com back in ’24, when the car sold last.
"First time I dropped the hammer at 5,800RPM on a B-body Hemi car and rowed through the 4-speed, shifting at 7,200RPM in each gear, tripping through the quarter mile in 11 seconds….I got back to the pits, got out of the car and my legs were shaking from the experience. I feel lucky to have had raced these cars. I think several others in this group have had the experience. That’s why there is so much love for the “ugly” Mopars!"
Yeah, about that “ugly:” the man who won the online bid back then wrapped up his experience with this gem: “Amazing, ugly car, big price.” I guess “ugly” is a new word for "great"?
Showing 84,727 miles on the odometer and backed by its original broadcast sheet, window sticker, National Hemi Owners Association records, and Galen Govier registry certificates, RM21J9G172560 possesses ironclad provenance. Even so, watching its price climb from a $130,000 sale in 2018 to $180,000 in January 2024 and a $250,000 asking figure since April 2025 explains why this 1-of-1 Ivy Green Metallic bruiser is still waiting for a buyer.

Jay Leno Drives Jerry O'Connell's 1979 Cadillac Seville, Stolen From His Driveway and Recovered
13 photos
Photo: Jay Leno's Garage | YouTube
Actor Jerry O’Connell took his 1979 Cadillac Seville to Jay Leno’s Garage to brag about it and to tell the story of how it was stolen from his driveway in California, pulled over for speeding, and recovered a few hours later, even before the actor realized it was missing.
The 1979 Cadillac Seville was stolen from Jerry O'Connell's driveway in Calabasas, California, on January 13 or 14, 2026, and recovered by law enforcement soon after the theft. The perpetrator got their hands on it while Jerry O’Connell and his wife, Rebecca Romijn, were out of town.
He had to pay for three days of impound, until authorities completed the investigation. The impound lot's chalk marks are still on the rear window. He later admitted he had left the keys inside the center console, so it was easy for the thief to drive off in it.
Deputies from the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department in Malibu pulled the car over for speeding at around 90 mph (145 kph). They found it hard to believe that a man like that would drive such a car. The thief was on a joyride on the Pacific Coast Highway.
When questioned, the driver claimed the vintage car belonged to him and grabbed whatever was in the glove box and handed it over as a bluff. Deputies ran the vehicle's registration, called the owner, and told him it had been stolen. The man was arrested, booked at the Malibu/Lost Hills Station, and later released on a promise to appear in court.
Days after the incident, O'Connell hilariously cleared up any confusion on social media, repeatedly posting headlines of the incident and telling his followers: " Just to be clear, I am not the homeless man in this story ."
Officers safely returned the car to its rightful owner, who publicly thanked the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department on social media, taking full responsibility for leaving the keys inside. That’s something he no longer does. He had never driven as fast as the thief before, but he is doing it now.
His Cadillac luxury sedan , finished in light blue, is his daily commuter car. He found it on Craigslist, where an older gentleman had it listed for sale for $16,000. He negotiated with the seller and eventually took it home for $12,000.
His wife, Rebecca, always acts as the witness during his strict classic-car buying process, which mandates only cars sold on Craigslist, located within 50 miles (80 kilometers) of home, and only models between 1960 and 1991.
He is 52 now, and Rebecca says he is only looking for cars rich people had when he was a child. He never buys a car she doesn’t approve of. His kids don’t get sick when they ride in the back, so that, along with the comfort and luxury it provides, convinced him to use it as a daily driver.
And speaking of comfort, Jerry sits on a wooden bead seat cushion. " There is nobody under the age of 70 sitting on one of these, " says 76-year-old Jay Leno . Jerry says he no longer drives without it. It's not just about comfort. The truth is that the driver's seat has started to show its age and he is masking it with the wooden bead seat cushion.
Jerry admits he washed the car for the show, but failed to clean the engine bay. “It’s the dustiest engine compartment I’ve ever seen,” Leno scolds him. “Are you driving in the desert or somewhere?” It actually looks like the engine compartment of a daily driver. Garaged collector cars that are only driven every once in a while are obviously far cleaner.
No wonder the Cadillac Seville got the homeless man's attention. The 1979 model year marked the grand finale for the first generation. When it debuted, the Cadillac-badged luxo-barge basically flipped American luxury car design on its head.
In the mid-1970s, American luxury meant massive land yachts. Cadillac introduced the Seville to fight back against rising European imports from luxury carmakers such as Mercedes-Benz and BMW. The Seville was 27 inches shorter and 1,000 pounds lighter than the standard DeVille.
Despite being far smaller, it was actually the automaker’s most expensive production car at the time, carrying a base price of roughly $15,600. Adjusted for inflation, that would be approximately $70,000 in today’s money.
The Seville was way ahead of its time. It pioneered GM’s early electronic fuel injection system and was available with the then-new digital Trip Computer dashboard, offered for extra money. A rear defogger and cruise control were also on the menu.
Powering the Seville is a 350-cubic-inch (5.7-liter) Oldsmobile Rocket V8 engine , which pushes out 170 horsepower (172 metric horsepower) and 270 pound-feet (366 Newton meters) of torque. A three-speed Turbo Hydra-Matic automatic transmission puts the power down through the rear wheels.
The Seville took forever to hit 60 mph (97 kph) from a standstill: it needed 13 seconds for the run on its way to a top speed of 115 mph (185 kph). But the Seville was more about luxury than about performance.
The car measures 204.0 inches (5,182 millimeters) in length, 71.8 inches (1,824 millimeters) in width, 54.7 inches (1,389 millimeters) in height, sitting on a wheelbase of 114.3 inches (2,903 millimeters). The Seville tips the scales at 4,180 pounds (1,896 kilograms).
That is what Jay Leno takes to the streets of Los Angeles. The suspension of the 47-year-old luxury sedan absorbs all the road imperfections for a plush-like ride, providing what Leno calls " a boulevard ride ."
" It's got some power, it’s kind of fun ," he says about the V8-powered luxo-barge from the 1970s. However, he doesn't go over 60 mph (97 kph). He won't drive it like he stole it.

BMW’s new iX5 is hard to miss with its distinct Double-X headlights. Here’s how it stacks up against the outgoing X5, side by side.
BMW upgrades fifth-gen X5 with the iX5
The X5 is among BMW’s best-selling vehicles in the US. In its fifth generation, it will be available across five powertrains.
In the US, it will be offered in gas, plug-in hybrid (PHEV), and, for the first time, battery electric (EV) powertrains. Other markets will also see diesel and hydrogen fuel cell variants.
The gas-powered 2027 X5 40 xDrive is now available, starting at $72,100, but the electric iX5 won’t go on sale until November.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Ahead of its official launch next month, Bimmertoday posted several images of the new iX5 parked next to the outgoing X5 G05, giving us a good side-by-side comparison.
Although it still looks like an X5, the new iX5 stands apart with BMW’s Neue Klasse design. The new upright, slimmer BMW Kidney Grille replaces the old wide, chunkier grille design.
View this post on Instagram A post shared by bimmertoday (@bimmertoday)
You can also see BMW’s new “double-X” light signature, which combines the headlights, daytime running lights, side lights, and turn signals into one unit. The Double-X headlights come standard, but BMW said you can turn them off for simpler diagonal stripes.
The new BMW iX5 60 xDrive will go on sale in the US next month. Using a 144 kWh battery, BMW said the electric SUV will offer up to 435 miles of range.
BMW iX5 60 xDrive hits 460 kW (Source: BMW)
Last week, BMW showcased the i5’s fast-charging capabilities for the first time during a media event in Southern California with IONNA and Alpitronic. During the event, the iX5 60 xDrive hit a peak of 464 kW, which BMW said enables it to add up to 170 miles of range in 10 minutes.
The iX5 is powered by a dual-motor all-wheel-drive powertrain, delivering a combined 578 hp (425 kW) and 593 lb-ft of torque. BMW says it can go from 0 to 60 mph in 4.4 seconds and tow up to 6,000 lbs.
BMW iX5 60 xDrive interior with M Sport Package (Source: BMW)
Inside, the iX5 adopts BMW’s Neue Klasse design, which includes a 17.9″ navigation touchscreen and the new BMW Panoramic Vision that stretches across the bottom of the windshield. Buyers can opt to add the optional 14.6″ passenger screen for a third display.
BMW’s new iX5 is 197.2″ long, 78.7″ wide, and 68.9″ tall, or about the size of the Porsche Cayenne Electric.
BMW iX5 60 xDrive interior with M Sport Package (Source: BMW)
BMW will open orders for the new iX5 60 xDrive in November, starting at $79,800. It will be BMW’s first electric vehicle built in the US. Production is set to begin at its Plant Spartanburg in South Carolina by the end of the year.

1969 Firebird Sprint Is Rarer Than Trans Ams, Needs Lots of TLC, Owner Wants To Know What It's Worth
15 photos
Photo: Craigslist
The phrase “1969 Firebird” almost immediately triggers thoughts of high-revving 400-cubic-inch eight-cylinder heavy-hitters, Ram Air induction setups, and the legendary debut of the Trans Am package in 1969. However, buried deep within the history of the Pontiac Motor Division lies a fascinating mechanical anomaly that defied conventional Detroit engineering dogma. One that actually ended in the last year of the sixties. And this Firebird OHC proudly wears it to this day.
The subject is a 1969 Pontiac Firebird coupe finished in black (a very matted, worn, weathered, and patina’ed kind of black), showing 100,000 miles on the odometer. According to the owner, the pony car retains its factory-installed engine and automatic transmission, and it left the assembly line equipped with the elusive “Sprint” performance package.
What that is/was? An exercise in Europeanization, coming off the drawing boards and think tanks of the most Euro-prone General Motors division of them all: Pontiac. After Semon Knudsen transitioned the “old man’s car” of the early fifties into the performance powerhouse of the early sixties, Pontiac’s own John Zachary DeLorean decided a heavy dose of Old World flair was in order.
The GTO would be the immediate example, but there have been other attempts (anyone remember the Banshee prototype?). However, badges and monikers alone wouldn’t cut it, so the ambitious manager took on a new challenge: revolutionize the Detroit school of thought right from the core of its beating heart. Which, in Yank terms, means making a pushrod V8 feel embarrassed of itself. Enter the OHC-6.
Photo: Craigslist “Over-Head Camshaft,” six-in-a-row. What more European than that could Pontiac go? V12 would be a good answer. However, Pontiac went only halfway, and stopped at six cylinders. It’s not that the idea was new to Motor City (Sixes had been around for a long while). It was the trickery of the missing pushrods that made the engine so exotic.
And it’s precisely that exact element that makes the car in the gallery so rare to begin with – and quite significant, if we consider that there were no more OHCs straight-sixes made by Pontiac after that model year. In fact, it would be more than three decades before GM considered another go at the idea, with the Vortec 4200 of the Atlas family of engines. More recently, the Mopar “Hurricane” (introduced in 2021 as the SIXPACK) put a new twist on the six-decade-old idea.
However, for full historic disclosure, let’s give full credit to Kaiser-Jeep for introducing the OHC Six in mass production, in 1962. The “Tornado” was a 230-cubic-inch SOHC straight-six engine featuring a hemi-head design, and a single, six-lobe camshaft for the transversally-opposed valves. That’s right, each lobe opened both the intake and the exhaust valves.
Photo: Craigslist The Jeep Tornado engine holds the distinction of being the only engine completely designed, developed, and built by Kaiser-Jeep during its ownership of the brand. Maybe John DeLorean had found inspiration nearby, and not all the way across the Atlantic, after all? Who knows? One thing is certain. Jeep retired the civilian version at the end of 1965, because the engine was far too demanding in terms of high-grade maintenance.
Back to the car in the gallery. It’s a rough ’69 Firebird, and it’s also a very rare one. How rare – and why so rare? Precisely because of that elusive powerplant, easily identified by the unmistakable die-cast aluminum cam housing.
That one-of-a-kind piece is the telltale of the Pontiac Overhead Cam. Debuting for the 1966 model year and ending production after 1969, this powerplant replaced the aging Chevrolet-designed pushrod inline-6. Over its four-year lifespan, the engine exclusively powered the intermediate A-body line—comprising the Tempest, Tempest Custom, Safari wagon, and LeMans—alongside the F-body Firebird from its February 1967 introduction through 1969.
Photo: Craigslist Instead of traditional pushrods and rocker arms, the engine utilized a single overhead camshaft driven by an external, fiberglass-reinforced neoprene toothed timing belt. That last bit was an industry first for an American mass-production powerplant – and the engine’s Achille’s heel. Stationary hydraulic lash adjusters acted as pivots for hardened iron cam followers. Initially displacing 230 cubic inches in 1966 and 1967 (coincidence with the Jeep Tornado?), the block was stroked for 1968 and 1969 to reach 250 cubic inches (4.1 liters).
While the standard 1969 OHC-6 inhaled through a single-barrel Rochester Monojet carburetor to produce 175 horsepower at 4,800 rpm and 240 lb-ft of torque at 2,600 rpm with a 9.0:1 compression ratio, the W53 “Sprint” option transformed its character. The upgrade added a four-barrel Rochester Quadrajet carburetor, a dual-cast split exhaust manifold, stiffer dual valve springs, a heavy-duty floor-shifted transmission, and a 10.5:1 compression ratio.
For the 1969 model year, the 250-cubic-inch engine featured a 3.875-inch bore and a 3.525-inch stroke. Interestingly, Pontiac calibrated the 1969 Sprint engine differently depending on the selected gearbox. Models paired with the manual 3- or 4-speed transmissions received an aggressive camshaft with 260 degrees of duration and 0.438-inch lift, generating a factory rating of 230 horsepower at 5,400 rpm and 260 lb-ft of torque at 3,600 rpm.
Photo: Craigslist Conversely, when buyers ordered a 1969 Sprint with an automatic transmission—either the 2-speed Super Turbine 300 or the 3-speed Turbo Hydra-Matic 350—Pontiac installed a slightly milder camshaft featuring 244 degrees of duration and 0.438-inch lift. This specific automatic configuration, which powers the coupe featured here, delivered 215 horsepower at 5,200 rpm and 255 lb-ft of torque at 3,800 rpm, offering smoother low-end idling in gear.
Across the entire first-generation run of 277,380 Firebirds, only 57,051 examples left the factory with any variant of the OHC-6. That total breaks down into 17,664 units in 1967 (out of 82,560 Firebirds), 18,494 units in 1968 (out of 107,112), and 20,893 units in 1969 (out of 87,708). Out of that three-year total, the high-compression Sprint package accounted for roughly 13,352 cars, representing under 5% of production.
Breaking down the Sprint figures by year and configuration highlights the scarcity of this car. In 1967, Pontiac built 7,210 Firebird Sprints across coupes and convertibles, split between 5,316 manual-shift cars and 1,894 automatics. For 1968, Sprint orders dropped to 4,662 units, comprising 4,005 hardtop coupes and 657 convertibles. By 1969, as buyers overwhelmingly favored eight-cylinder power, Sprint production plummeted to 1,979 units (267 of them convertibles).
Photo: Craigslist Within the 1969 OHC-6 lineup of 20,893 Firebirds, the vast majority were base 175-horsepower coupes and convertibles equipped with automatic transmissions. Across all 1969 Pontiac lines, factory engine records show just 3,242 Sprint 250 blocks assembled: 2,357 manual-transmission ZH-code engines and 885 automatic-transmission ZL-code units.
For the 1969 Firebird Sprint specifically, only 54 convertibles were built with automatic gearboxes, out of the 267 total ragtop Sprints, while automatic Sprint coupes accounted for just 428 copies. The manuals reached 1,284 units. If you really want to go down the production stats rabbit hole, hold on tight: of the total of 1,712 Firebird coupe Sprints assembled for the 1969 model year, only 397 came from the Norwood facility in Ohio. This is one of the 94 automatics made there.
The Lordstown , OH, plant takes the crown, with 887 coupes (237 autos), while the Van Nuys, California assembly lines left out 428 solid-roof Sprints (97 with a self-shifting cogbox).
Photo: Craigslist Back in the day, contemporary automotive publications praised the Firebird Sprint for its balanced weight distribution and nimble front-end handling compared to nose-heavy eight-cylinder counterparts. Period road tests of 4-speed Sprint models recorded 0-to-60 mph sprints in 7.8 to 8.2 seconds and standing quarter-mile runs of 16.0 seconds at 88 mph, with a top speed of 124 mph, while automatic and convertible variants clocked high-18s quarter-mile passes.
So this car is rarer than a same-year Trans Am. It’s also a lot less valuable, which may have a lot to do with the condition. The pictures are speaking volumes – this car was not loved, not one bit. The most noticeable structural flaw is the caved-in rear quarter on the driver’s side. The owner points out that a replacement stamping is already in transit.
Photo: Craigslist There is rust and dust and missing paint and saggy rear-right wheel lip molding, but the glass, stainless window trim, and rear valance appear solid. Inside the cabin, the dashboard and door panels with integrated armrests look complete, and the seats are in surprising good shape, too. The engine and transmission are original, and the condition is described as “pretty close to original.”
Its current residence is Spokane, WA, and the owner is asking $15k for it. But that’s just shaking the tree to see how many monkeys fall off – he doesn’t really need to sell. However, he may be off the mark with that value, as many gearheads don’t have good words about the OHC-6’s tendency to fall out of sync once the timing belt elongated past the point of elasticity, resulting in a bad timing and all the other associated headaches. So, what do you think this is worth?

This Unique Travel Trailer Concept Still Stands Out After Five Years of Being Active – It's Flawless
15 photos
Photo: Arina Arkharova
Some camper designs are just so beautiful and well-executed that they transcend time, and the concept before us today is precisely one of those campers. Keep in mind that it first showed up in 2021, so it’s been five years, and if I may, the Rush Camper, as it’s called, is just as welcome today as ever. Heck, it’ll be just as welcome in five years from now, and I'm willing to bet that even five years after that.
Folks, the Rush Camper (RC) is a concept from the mind of Arina Arkharova, an industrial designer from Russia, and while this concept hit the scene back in 2021, it's so damn good and out-there, displaying tricks that very few, if any, campers ever showcase, that I just couldn’t resist bringing it to light; you’ll thank me later.
Now, the entire presentation page I encountered for this thing is all in Russian, so I couldn’t understand a darned thing, but what is clear is what this camper brings to the table, and if I may, all of it transcends language.
Photo: Arina Arkharova Starting off with the exterior, Arina has given rise to a camper that runs fluid and seamless from tip to tail, at least, particular sections of the body, the proper way to design an RV so that it stands the test of time. It also looks clean and very modern, especially when we throw in that sweeping windshield at the front.
But, and this is where things get interesting. If we look closely at the roof of the RC, we can see that it features a few separate panels at the rear, signaled by the seams we see running along the edge of the roof. The same is true for the lower half of the body, and the silver seam we see does highlight a particular ability, and it’s the one that makes this camper so special.
Once you’ve made it to camp , the upper and lower sections of the rear unfold to create a little patio section with overhang, placing us in the presence of the kitchen nearby, allowing us to cook meals from outside, but also opening up the interior to the world outside, letting fresh air and the sun’s rays inside. Talk about cooking with a view.
Photo: Arina Arkharova That kitchen is also one that’s very modern with sleek and curved edges, flowing countertop space with integrated appliances, including a cooktop, sink with faucet, fridge, and lighting from above that rains down on the entire space. I think it looks fantastic, but I'm curious to hear what you think about this area of the concept.
Once you’ve cooked your meal, you can enjoy it right then and there by simply plopping down on the lower section but Arina also added an awning along the camping side of the RC where we’ll also set up a couple of chairs and dining table.
One trait that some folks, myself included, may see as a downside is the lack of being able to step inside via the kitchen; it would have been a simple solution, like installing a hinged section of countertop.
Entry inside the RC is to be made via the right side of the unit through an oddly shaped door that will require larger folks to turn to the side to enter. Once in, to our right, or under that sweeping windshield, is a modular lounge with two opposing benches and central table that transform into a bed at night. A drop-down bed is also spotted in the ideation board too.
Photo: Arina Arkharova But, as we head toward the rear, or the kitchen, we can see a couple of larger cubicles standing in the center. One of these cubicles is nothing but storage, but the other is a wet bath, ready with vanity, shower, and a hideaway toilet.
It literally has all the features a family, couple, and single travellers would need to live off the land. It doesn’t matter how much water is in place here or how much this camper weighs – it is concept after all – or the AC, heating, and plumbing and electrical, but the styling that Arina has implemented is gorgeous.
It’s not often we see a camper that looks this simple but has so much goodness and functionality, reason why I chose to bring this concept to light, even five years after it was originally showcased. Heck, if we look closely, we can even see that this one is designed with an independent suspension system, trailing A-arm and all and solar off-grid power is also in the works.
Photo: Arina Arkharova Frankly, everything I see here is just as applicable today as ever, and it’s sure to be just as applicable years down the line, especially with the way trends are moving.
Lately, countless brands have been choosing to create RVs with flush bodies, movable parts, and interiors that feel more like yachts than grandma and grandpa’s travel trailers. Personally, I wouldn’t be the least bit surprised to see a camper like the RC on the market in the coming years.
I’d love to see one in real life but am curious to hear your thoughts on this concept; is it one you’d be seen towing behind your vehicle?

Jeep Gladiator Is Finally Getting the Feature That Customers Have Always Wanted
8 photos
Photo: Jeep
It is finally happening. Jeep has officially answered one of the most common aftermarket requests from truck enthusiasts by introducing the limited-production 2027 Jeep Gladiator 35-inch Tire Launch Edition, which comes with upgraded off-road credentials and bronze accents that set it apart from its siblings.
Owners had to seek out larger tires via aftermarket shops, often putting their warranties at risk in order to make their off-roaders more off-road capable. But now, things are about to change as the new package will give the Gladiator a more aggressive stance. The new package delivers the heavy-duty upgrades that they have always wanted right off the factory floor.
Available for orders across North America on Willys, Rubicon, and Rubicon X trim levels, this package pairs enhanced mechanicals with exclusive visual details. But the best part of the plan is squeezing massive 35-inch rubber onto the midsize truck, which requires structural adjustments to maintain handling and durability.
Jeep completely reworked the chassis and drivetrain by integrating several key components. They came up with a factory-engineered one-inch suspension lift to provide clearance for the new larger tires. Highline fender flares and wheel-flare extensions prevent tire rub during extreme wheel articulation.
Photo: Jeep Furthermore, they paired 4.56 final-drive ratios with a full-time 4:1 low-range transfer case to restore low-speed crawling precision and throttle responsiveness. The 35-inch Tire Package includes heavy-duty Dana solid axles and upgraded performance brakes.
Riding on the 17-inch beadlock-capable wheels with the all-new 35-inch all-terrain tires, the Jeep Gladiator 35-inch Tire Launch Edition raises the bar for the truck’s factory Trail Rated capability. The Gladiator now comes with an impressive 12.9 inches of ground clearance, an approach angle of 46.7 degrees, a breakover angle of 23.3 degrees, and a departure angle of 26.7 degrees.
To make the special edition instantly recognizable, Jeep came up with bronze accents. The 17-inch wheels sport a bronze finish, matching the bronze front tow hooks and the exclusive bronze Jeep badging, accompanied by bespoke hood, side, and tailgate graphics.
The Rubicon and Rubicon X trims add extra vent graphics, while the range-topping Rubicon X package further includes a sculpted Jeep performance hood and unique side decals.
Photo: Jeep Customers can already go ahead and order the 2027 Jeep Gladiator 35-inch Tire Launch Edition anywhere across North America. Jeep hasn’t disclosed the pricing of the new package, but if the XTREME 35-Inch Tire Package available for the Wrangler is anything to go by, customers should expect to pay around $4,495 on top of the price of each trim that it comes with.
The 2027 Jeep Gladiator Willys starts at $49,040, the Gladiator Rubicon costs $55,700, while the Rubicon X is a $64,120 deal.

BYD’s upcoming flagship EV will be its largest and most luxurious electric sedan yet, potentially debuting two firsts for the company: Rolls-Royce-style coach doors and solid-state batteries.
BYD will unveil its new flagship electric sedan in the UAE
BYD is better known for its low-cost electric cars, like the Seagull , a little hatchback that sells for under $10,000 in China.
The Chinese auto giant has greatly expanded its portfolio over the past few months and years. BYD now offers everything from entry-level EVs to three-row flagship SUVs, pickup trucks, electric supercars, and just about everything in between.
BYD has three sub-brands: Denza, FangChengBao, and Yangwang. It also has two main families under the BYD brand: the Dynasty and Ocean series.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Yangwang sits at the top of BYD’s brand hierarchy and showcases its latest breakthrough technologies.
Previously, Yangwang vehicles debuted on BYD’s quad-motor e4 platform, delivering a whopping 1,300 horsepower and featuring its DiSus-X intelligent body control system, which enables the vehicle to “dance,” jump, and drive on three wheels.
BYD Yangwang flagship sedan prototype (Source: Hu Xiaoqing)
For its next model, BYD is pushing further into the elite segment to take on ultra-luxury brands like Rolls-Royce, Bentley, and Mercedes-Maybach.
Yangwang general manager Hu Xiaoqing revealed several images of its new executive sedan testing last month.
BYD Yangwang flagship sedan prototype (Source: Hu Xiaoqing)
Although it was disguised, it appeared to be about the same shape and size as the Mercedes-Benz Maybach S-Class or Rolls-Royce Phantom. Local reports indicate it will be around 5,500 mm (216″) long.
HU confirmed for the first time last week that the global launch of the new flagship sedan will take place in the UAE, not in BYD’s home market of China.
BYD has not yet revealed a specific launch date, but the Yangwang sedan could make its first appearance as early as next week. According to CarNewsChina , citing “sources familiar with the project,” BYD is aiming to reveal the new flagship model in Dubai, UAE, around November 5.
Yangwang flagship electric sedan (Source: Zheng Yu)
Zheng Yu, Yangwang’s executive general manager, said the new model will feature “unprecedented disruptive technology,” but didn’t reveal specifics.
Although details are still limited, the ultra-luxury sedan was shown at BYD’s Flash Charging station, suggesting it will support megawatt flash charging.
It also features rear-hinged coach doors, a first for BYD. The flagship EV will reportedly be the first to feature BYD’s solid-state batteries.
BYD executive vice president Stella Li said during an interview with Carwow.es last month that the company’s first vehicle to use solid-state batteries will debut in 2027.
Li said BYD is “in the leading position” in solid-state battery technology and its commercialization, and the company plans to prove it next year.
BYD Yangwang executive sedan prototype testing (Source: Zheng Yu)
BYD’s battery unit, FinDreams, plans to begin production of sulfide-based all-solid-state batteries in 2027. It will initially be produced in limited batches, then scale to mass production closer to the end of the decade.
While BYD has yet to confirm it, introducing the new battery tech in a flagship model would make sense.
The executive sedan is expected to debut around November 5. Prices are rumored to start in the 2 million yuan range, or about $300,000.
Yangwang’s current electric sedan, the U7, starts at 658,000 yuan ($98,000). The brand also sells the U8 (and U8L), a plug-in hybrid luxury off-road SUV, and the U9, a fully electric super-coupe.
The extended U8L is Yangwang’s highest-priced mass-produced vehicle, starting at 1.45 million yuan ($217,000).

Since 2025, U.S. biopharma companies have raised $37.2 billion—68% of total worldwide venture capital funding—with startups in the San Francisco Bay Area and Boston leading the way.
Biopharma has collected $54.5 billion across 959 rounds globally since the start of 2025 through 2026’s third quarter, with U.S. companies attracting $37.2 billion—about 68% of the total funding.
In the U.S., the two leading biopharma hubs are the San Francisco Bay Area and Boston, raising $12.8 billion and $10.2 billion since 2025, respectively, according to an October biopharma report from J.P. Morgan. Together, the two areas gathered about 62% of all U.S. biopharma funding over the past seven quarters, “underscoring the continued concentration of capital in established life-sciences ecosystems,” according to the report.
San Diego, Philadelphia and the Research Triangle in North Carolina stood out as three other strong U.S. fundraisers, raising a collective $5.2 billion over the same time period.
Outside of the U.S., European biopharma companies raised $9.2 billion from 2025 to 2026’s Q3, accounting for just under 17% of all capital deployed. In Europe, the U.K. raised the largest share, securing $3.1 billion across 58 rounds. Switzerland followed at $1.8 billion, with France drawing in $851 million and Germany raising $832 million.
Worldwide, money deployed in the most recent quarter stayed concentrated in fewer, larger rounds. Half of the $1.1 billion in capital deployed came from just five of the 32 rounds.
Overall, 2026 is on track to surpass last year’s total of $30.5 billion, with J.P. Morgan projecting full-year biopharma funding to reach about $33 billion.

This Single-Level Tiny House Is a Charming Personal Oasis for Minimalist Living
27 photos
Photo: Be Tiny Homes/ Exploring Alternatives
Soaring housing prices in many parts of the world continue to motivate more people to adopt small-scale living as an affordable alternative to traditional housing. And as demand for tiny houses continues to grow, new builders are entering the market. The latest I’ve come across is Be Tiny Homes, a company based in Quebec, Canada.
Be Tiny Homes has been in operation for two years and offers several models designed for different uses, from hospitality pods and accessory dwelling units to tiny houses on wheels. It was founded by a couple with over 15 years of experience in real estate who wanted to create a project that better aligned with their love for nature and environmental consciousness.
The company builds modern, high-quality tiny houses made with durable and mostly locally-sourced materials, aiming to offer downsizers both the simplicity of tiny living and the comfort and convenience of a traditional house.
The B.Drop.24F is the first model the company completed and combines beautiful, warm finishes with a remarkably functional layout. Suitable for downsizers who prefer single-level living, this tiny home is a one-story model designed to accommodate two people seeking simple, minimalist living.
Photo: Be Tiny Homes/ Exploring Alternatives It measures 24 feet (7.3 meters) long and 8.5 feet (2.6 meters) wide, and it can be built on a trailer on wheels for those who want the ability to tow their home everywhere, but it can also be set up on a plot of land. Built on a steel frame base, the home boasts a beautiful exterior clad in spruce siding with an accent wall made of cedar posts. The use of light-toned natural wood gives it a sense of tranquility that instantly evokes luxurious vacation retreat vibes.
The unit pictured here is accompanied by a tiered wooden deck that leads to extra-wide patio doors, perfect for allowing natural light to fill the interior and creating the coveted indoor-outdoor connection. Once you step inside, you discover a space that feels organic, warm and serene, while also providing remarkable functionality.
Described as an “aesthetically elevated product,” the B.Drop.24F boasts a charming retro-inspired interior dominated by neutral beiges and grays and natural materials that give it an earthy feel. The light walls and ceilings, covered in Russian birch plywood with lime paint, are complemented by cork flooring, while the quartz countertops and a stone sink contribute to the overall natural vibe. Curved edges and soft lines are used throughout, creating a calming, fluid look.
Photo: Be Tiny Homes/ Exploring Alternatives As stylish as it looks, this home is meant for efficient everyday living. It’s the kind of space that doesn’t need to be expansive to be livable and practical. The layout is nothing out of the ordinary, with a central living and cooking area flanked by a sleeping space on one side and the bathroom on the other. But the arrangement is different from other studio-style tiny houses , as it puts an elevated queen-size bed in a dedicated alcove behind an arched divider wall and reserves the rest of the space for a proper kitchen and a welcoming lounge.
The bedroom is accessed by a pair of stairs that also serve as storage. It is a true oasis for rest and relaxation, with a comfy mattress, privacy curtains, and an awning-style picture window for beautiful views of nature. Overhead cabinets add some storage for clothes, and the raised bed also has storage underneath, which can be accessed through a hatch from the outside of the house.
A custom-built L-shaped sofa is positioned in front of the bed, creating a sunken feel. It features recessed LED lighting underneath to create a nice ambiance, while a small wood-burning stove next to it brings the warmth and coziness of a mountain cabin.
Photo: Be Tiny Homes/ Exploring Alternatives The kitchen occupies three-thirds of the home’s width and includes everything you find in a conventional house but on a smaller scale. You get a mini fridge, a two-burner stovetop, a toaster oven, and a stone sink. A kitchen peninsula creates a sense of separation between the lounge and the cooking area, while also adding extra meal-prep area and a space for dining.
Despite the compactness of the kitchen, there is ample storage thanks to lower and upper cabinets, storage built into the kitchen island, and two additional shelves above the bathroom door frame.
Speaking of the bathroom, it represents another proof of the company’s attention to detail. It’s a compact room, but it includes all the necessary fixtures, such as a small toilet, a semi-oval ceramic sink, and a storage cabinet. But the standout feature is the generous 3-by-3-foot tiled shower with a recessed shelf for toiletries.

You shouldn't have to leave your family behind when traveling by camper van – you just need the right setup that can fit everybody comfortably. That's the type of conversion I'd like to share with you folks today.
Meet Salt Lake, a family-friendly build made by Summit Vans Australia, a Wollongong, Australia-based company specializing in deluxe, off-grid camper vans. We've covered several of its projects here on autoevolution, such as the Bamboo Basecamp .
Summit Vans shared that Salt Lake is its most capable family adventure van it has yet made. It's based on a 2025 AWD Mercedes-Benz Sprinter with, surprisingly, a 144" wheelbase. I say surprisingly because you'd expect a family camper van to be based on the long wheelbase version of the Sprinter, not the shorter one.
As usual, let's first take a look at the exterior. The vehicle rides on 17-inch Summit wheels wrapped in all-terrain tires. Summit Vans improved the van's stock off-roading capabilities by fitting Fox Factory Race front struts and rear shocks. It also added heavy-duty rear leaf springs and raised the GVM (Gross Vehicle Mass) capabilities to 4,430 kg (9,766 lb.).
At the rear, you'll come across a spare tire carrier/ladder combo and another carrier holding two bike racks and traction boards. On the opposite end, the builders fitted an Aluminess Recon bumper complete with a Warn winch and a bullbar holding two Baja Designs LP6 light pods.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Summit Vans Australia On the driver's side, Summit Vans installed a surfboard mount next to a ladder that offers quick and easy access to the roof. There, you'll come across a Weldbeat rack holding five front-facing Baja Designs LP9 light pods (three clear and two amber) and a Fiamma F45S awning.
The roof also has the most significant exterior mod : an Alucab LT-50. It's a lightweight pop-top tent that tips the scales at a mere 101 lb. (46 kg). Moreover, it has a low-profile aluminum shell with a streamlined profile for wind resistance, a UV-resistant canvas, and foam insulation.
The tent offers three zipped windows and a plush 60mm-thick foam mattress. On top of the tent, there's a 410 W solar panel.
Other notable mods are a Bravo snorkel, power and water connections, heavy-duty side steps, and a set of flares. Furthermore, the bumper and lower rocker panels are coated in Raptor truck bed liner for an extra layer of protection.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Summit Vans Australia Flares, also known as pods or capsules, are designed to increase the van width to allow you to fit a bed inside from side to side instead of front to back. This rig's flares are paint matched to the van's body and come with small awning-style windows.
Stepping inside, a masterfully crafted interior will greet you. I love the darker design consisting of black laminated cabinetry, 2tec2 woven vinyl flooring, and a matching ceiling with recessed LED light strips and a bamboo center strip. The look is complemented by a white solid surface countertop.
The interior has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space. Moreover, the driver and passenger seats are mounted on swivel bases, allowing you to turn them around to face the back of the van.
The kitchen sits dead ahead of the entrance. It features a deep stainless steel sink with a cover, a microwave oven, and an 85-liter Dometic fridge with a tiny freezer compartment.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Summit Vans Australia An overhead cabinet, five drawers with soft-close mechanisms, a shoe cubby, and a cabinet underneath the sink are available for storage.
Next, we have the main seating area in the middle part of the living space. It's a three-seater Techsafe bench complete with seatbelts and a Lagun table mount.
Finally, we have the bedroom in the back – it's a fixed sleeping arrangement with a queen-size mattress. In addition, you'll notice two overhead cabinets, two shelves, two reading lights, and L-Tracks on the side walls that serve as mounting points. One of the L-Tracks holds a Sirocco swivel fan.
Underneath the bedroom, you'll find a garage that's accessible only from outside the van after opening the two rear doors. In the middle, there's a heavy-duty pull-out tray that makes it easier to load and unload items. It also has a fork mount for storing a mountain bike.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Summit Vans Australia Power is on the left side – the electrical system's highlights are an 820 Ah lithium battery bank and a 3,000 W inverter. Three charging sources are available: solar power , shore power, and DC-DC charging while the engine is running.
As for plumbing, the van is equipped with a 180-liter (47-gallon) freshwater tank, a water filtration system, and an outdoor shower connection. The last important system is a Dieselheat DH9 hydronic system offering both heated air and hot water.
All in all, Salt Lake by Summit Vans indeed makes family adventures comfortable regardless of where you go. It cleverly combines premium design, innovative systems, and serious off-grid capability.

Tesla Model 3 (Source: Tesla)
Tesla Canada has updated the Model 3 Premium Rear-Wheel Drive on its website with 584 km of range and a 0-100 km/h time of 5.2 seconds. Those are the exact specs of the Fremont-built Long Range RWD that Tesla sold in Canada two years ago.
The Shanghai-built version, the $39,490 CAD car Canadians haven’t been able to order since early October, is rated at 463 km and 6.2 seconds. The new numbers point to a different car from a different factory.
Canadian Tesla owner RJ was first to spot the change on X:
Tesla Canada 🇨🇦 has updated Model 3 Premium RWD range and 0-100 specs. New specs: 584 km range (previously 463 km) 0-100 in 5.2 seconds (previously 6.2 seconds) Note: Premium Model 3 RWD orders are currently paused because the Government of Canada states Tesla has exhausted its… pic.twitter.com/PeWP15w2RS — RJ (@RJTesla) October 26, 2026
The new figures are in the “Model 3 Premium Specs” section of Tesla’s Canadian Model 3 page, under the Rear-Wheel Drive tab, along with a curb weight of 1,745 kg. The page’s marketing copy now also promises “up to 584 km (EPA est.) on a single charge.”
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Tesla hasn’t touched its Canadian comparison page, though. As of this afternoon, it still lists the Model 3 Premium RWD at 463 km, 6.2 seconds and $39,490.
The specs match Fremont, not Shanghai
In October 2024, Tesla Canada listed the Model 3 Long Range RWD at 584 km and 5.2 seconds, starting at $54,990 and eligible for the federal iZEV rebate. That car came from Fremont.
They also line up with the Model 3 Premium RWD Tesla sells in the US today. Tesla’s US website rates it at 363 miles of EPA range, which converts to 584 km, with 0-60 mph in 4.9 seconds. It starts at $42,490 USD.
There’s one other candidate. Giga Shanghai builds a Model 3 Long Range RWD for the Chinese market with a 78.4 kWh pack, 830 km of CLTC range and the same 5.2-second 0-100 km/h time.
But a Shanghai-built car runs into the same quota problem that paused Model 3 orders in Canada earlier this month . Tesla’s website says orders will resume “if Govt of Canada issues more quota, expected March 2027.” Meanwhile, the federal tracker showed 33,069 of the period’s permits still unused as of October 9.
So if Tesla wants to sell a long-range Model 3 in Canada before March, it has to come from Fremont.
The tariff problem hasn’t gone away
And that’s where it gets expensive. Canada’s 25% counter-tariffs on US-made vehicles, in place since April 2025, still apply. The Department of Finance’s counter-tariff page, updated October 9, says the measures against US autos “continue to apply.”
Those tariffs are what pushed Tesla out of US-built Model 3s in the first place. When they hit, Tesla raised the Model 3 Long Range AWD by $11,000 to $79,990 and dropped the $55,990 RWD entirely. In March, it shipped its remaining US-built Model 3 inventory out of Canada ahead of the switch to Shanghai, which led to the record-low $39,490 Model 3 Premium RWD in May .
If Tesla applies a similar markup to a Fremont-built Premium RWD, it would land somewhere around $65,000 to $67,000. That’s well above the $50,000 transaction cap of Canada’s new $5,000 EV Affordability Program, even though US-built cars otherwise qualify through CUSMA (Chinese-built ones don’t).
Right now, the only Model 3 you can order in Canada is the Performance, which Tesla priced at $74,990 when it cut its price in May.
Electrek’s Take
Tesla hasn’t announced anything, and the configurator hasn’t changed. But Tesla doesn’t usually rewrite a spec sheet for a car it isn’t planning to sell, and these numbers match a car it has sold in Canada before.
The most logical explanation is a stopgap. Tesla had a real hit with the $39,490 Model 3, ran through its quota in about four months, and is now stuck selling a $75,000 Performance until March. A Fremont-built Premium RWD would give buyers a long-range Model 3 at something less painful than that.
The problem is that it’d be a tough sell. I think Canadian buyers are more likely to wait and see if Tesla gets more quotas next and year. At the same time, they will wait to see what the Chinese automakers have to offer next year.

Audi’s RS3 Gets a Redesign for 2028, Albeit Only Virtually
6 photos
Photo: Instagram | ap.studio.974
The fourth-generation Audi A3 blew six candles off its birthday cake a few months ago. The unveiling took place in March 2020 for the Sportback (hatchback), with the Sedan (four-door) model debuting one month later, and production commenced at the Ingolstadt factory in Germany in May 2020.
Besides its homeland, the model is also assembled at the Qingdao factory in China as part of the FAW-VW partnership, but only for the A3L. That’s the long wheelbase model available strictly in the People’s Republic, where new car buyers fancy rides that offer extra legroom for those sitting at the rear.
Offered in two body styles, as mentioned in the intro, the fourth-gen Audi A3 is based on the Volkswagen Group’s MQB Evo platform. The construction is quite old, though extremely versatile, as it is also used by the Q3, Q6, Cupra Formentor and Terramar, SEAT Leon, Skoda Octavia, Superb, Kodiaq, Volkswagen Atlas / Teramont, Golf Mk8, Passat, Tiguan, Tayron, T-Roc, and other models.
Depending on where it is sold, the latest A3 can be had with an inline-three, an inline-four hybrid, a bi-fuel (gasoline / CNG) unit, a diesel for the Old Continent, and a straight-five. And the latter is clearly reserved for the RS 3 lineup. The RS 3 Sportback may not be available on our shores, but the RS 3 Sedan is, and has an MSRP of $67,500 for the 2027 model year, whereas the lesser S3 Sedan starts at $52,500, and the normal A3 Sedan at $40,700.
Photo: Instagram | ap.studio.974 The latter does 0-60 mph (0-97 kph) in 6.0 seconds, and has 201 hp (204 ps/150 kW ) and 236 lb-ft (320 Nm) of torque to play with, whereas the S3 comes with 328 hp (333 ps/245 kW) and 295 lb-ft (400 Nm) of torque, and completes the acceleration in 4.4 seconds. The RS 3, on the other hand, completes the sprint in 3.6 seconds, which is roughly as fast as the iconic Ferrari Enzo. The 2.5L five-banger is officially good for 394 hp (400 ps/294 kW) and 369 pound-feet (500 Nm) of torque.
With this short history lesson behind us, it is now time to move on to the real reason behind this story, which is the facelifted Audi RS 3 Sportback mentioned in the title. And just like we previous said, it is a virtual project. What does that mean? That is is nothing more than a rendered machine, which was signed by @ap.studio.974 in this case and shared on social media while it was still summer in the northern hemisphere.
The CGI-infused model features a completely new front fascia. It has different headlights that are a lot more modern this time around, as well as a new bumper with a more aggressive styling, and an apron with blades on the sides attached to it. The side skirts and front fender trim are also new, and out back, we can see a different bumper, a new diffuser, and redesigned taillights that are much slimmer this time around, and are linked together by a thin light strip that stretches across the tailgate.
One single thing does not match the vibes of an RS model, because they all feature large dual oval tailpipes, yet this rendered Audi RS 3 Sportback has different ones sticking out from the new diffuser. The wheels are a lot bigger than the OEM ones, and the ground clearance appears to have been slightly altered, as this machine sits a bit closer to the asphalt. It has a gray paint finish, and the usual black accents.
Photo: Instagram | ap.studio.974 Unfortunately, the quoted pixel artist hasn’t imagined the car’s interior, too, but something like this would feature a few changes on the inside, too. These would at least include new screens, some revised switchgear, a modified center console, a new steering wheel, different trim and upholstery, probably new air vents, and a few other bits and bobs in order to make the car stand out more compared to its predecessor.
On top of these, some chassis tweaks could also be part of the makeover, and the powertrain would likely carry over, though some upgrades in this department could also be part of the car’s mid-cycle refresh, alongside new wheels, an expanded color palette, and a few other bits and bobs.
To be honest, I like the design of this rendered Audi RS 3 Sportback, and would like to see what its four-door sibling, namely the RS 3 Sedan that the four-ring brand sells on our shores, would look like with this CGI mods. The only things that I do not agree with are the tailpipes, which do not do justice to any RS model, and I also think that the side skirts are a bit too much, and the new wheels a bit too large. Other than these, we’ve got a winner, don’t we?
But do you also like the unofficial mid-cycle refresh of this model? View this post on Instagram A post shared by @ap.studio.974

Cadillac XT5 Is Off to a Good Start and This Is What America Is Missing
10 photos
Photo: 2027 Cadillac XT5 PHEV
The 2027 Cadillac XT5 PHEV is off to a strong start in China. The new variant racked up over 3,000 orders in just its first 17 days on the market after it was officially launched in early September. The XT5 is also available in the United States, but it is a completely different vehicle.
Offered in Air, Pro, and Pro Max trims, with higher-end trims launching first and the entry-level Air debuting in October, the Cadillac XT5 PHEV starts at 239,900 yuan, which translates to roughly $35,900. The U.S. XT5 is a $44,800 deal.
The Chinese Cadillac XT5 PHEV uses local tech, featuring the Momenta R7 driver-assistance system with a LiDAR sensor present on the higher trims. The plug-in variant pairs a 1.5-liter turbocharged inline-four engine with a dual-motor setup, operating in an all-wheel-drive layout.
A two-speed Direct Hybrid Transmission puts the power down through all four corners. The system pumps out 362 horsepower (367 metric horsepower) and 369 pound-feet (500 Newton meters) of torque for a run from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in 4.6 seconds on its way to a top speed of 130 mph (210 kph).
Photo: Cadillac China The Cadillac XT5 PHEV is equipped with a 35.5 kWh ternary lithium battery pack, which stores enough energy for a drive of 134 miles (215 kilometers) on electric power only under the very generous Chinese testing cycle.
The car features a highly advanced 5C charge rating, allowing it to charge from 30% to 80% in just 15 minutes using a compatible DC fast charger, and supports an external discharge capacity of up to 6 kW, meaning it can act as a mobile generator to power appliances, camping gear, or tools.
General Motors has no current plans to bring the China-engineered XT5 PHEV to North America, where the aging XT5 remains, even though it is sitting on an outdated platform. The XT5 made its debut on the U.S. market back in 2016 as a 2017 model year, which basically makes it a decade old with only minor updates.
The XT5 is thus one of the oldest luxury vehicles still on sale today. While Cadillac is selling an EREV and a PHEV in China, the American XT5 relies strictly on non-electrified combustion engines.
Photo: Cadillac USA The 2.0-liter turbocharged four-cylinder unit sits at the base of the lineup with 235 horsepower (238 metric horsepower) and 258 pound-feet (350 Newton meters) of torque. In the meantime, the 3.6-liter naturally aspirated V6 has to deal with 310 horsepower (314 metric horsepower) and 271 pound-feet (367 Newton meters) of torque.
There will not be a 2027 model-year XT5 in the US. Cadillac is completely pausing the nameplate for about nine months. In the meantime, General Motors will invest $275 million into its Spring Hill, Tennessee assembly plant, where the XT5 currently rolls off the production line. GM has reversed earlier plans to phase out the model and is reportedly planning a major next-generation update for North America.

Unboxing: 10 Hot Wheels From the '90s and Early 2000s I Bought in October 2026 (TH Inside)
143 photos
Photo: autoevolution
I’m not sure if the world around us is crazier by the day, or if it was always this way and we just didn’t realize it. After all, news wouldn’t spread so fast in the ‘90s for instance. Where I grew up, nobody even had an Internet connection back then. Some people didn’t even have a landline in their homes.
We could just go out and play games with our friends, with seemingly no worries in sight. Maybe it was just part of being a kid, while our parents had to figure out how to put food on the table the next day.
I couldn’t have imagined what 2026 would be like, spending at least eight to 10 hours a day in front of a screen (small or big).
So yes, I am nostalgic over the ‘90s as it was the most magical decade of my life. And I always love going back to that era by playing video games like WarCraft II and StarCraft, watching movies like Point Break and Ace Ventura, and listening to my favorite hits from that period.
In recent years I’ve discovered yet another method to relive my childhood through purchasing Hot Wheels collectibles that are almost as old as me.
Photo: autoevolution I worked on my first such story in August of 2025 , then had another go at it in April of this year. Luckily for me, I’ve found a supplier in my area that brings in old Mainline models and sells them for reasonable prices.
As a result, I’ve bought 20 more items from him this month, and I’m saving some for November.
You’ll notice the list is chronological based on the first release of each casting, starting in 1995 and going all the way up to 2002.
So play some era-appropriate music and enjoy the nostalgic trip we’re about to embark on together.
Dodge Ram 1500 Photo: autoevolution I’ve got two pickup trucks on my list for today, but I can definitely say the Dodge Ram 1500 is my favorite. It’s also one of two castings designed by Larry Wood here, and one of several that are First Edition releases.
That’s a big bonus for me, and I’m sure other collectors feel the same way. If you want some more interesting information, I can tell you this is Mattel ’s first-ever Ram truck.
A racing version of it followed suit in 1998, then a Tooned one showed up in 2004, but the next 1500 version appeared in 2007.
This Ram 1500 was collectible #7 for the 1995 Model Series, and I’ve previously unboxed the Hydroplane from the same selection.
Photo: autoevolution I should get the Ferrari 355 next. I realized I could probably take the bed cover off the moment I took it out from the blister card.
I had to use some force to get the job done and broke something in the process, but it hasn’t affected its “functionality”. The metallic green finish looks amazing, and it reminds me of the ‘97 Corvette I took photos of earlier this year.
The bed cover’s paint job is slightly different, which isn’t a deal breaker. Mattel also used the 5DOT wheels on this vehicle that same year, but I’d probably go after the two variations that were part of the 100% Preferred: Mopar Performance Parts series in 2003 (Real Riders!).
The Ram 1500 sadly went away in 2008, with the 40 Years of Hot Wheels Set that also included the GMC Motorhome, Volkswagen Drag Bus and the Twin Mill to name a few of the items inside.
1996 Ford Mustang GT Photo: autoevolution While there are nearly 40 variations of the Ram 1500 to chase after, the 1996 Ford Mustang GT wasn’t quite as successful.
You’ll only find roughly 20 of them, with some only changing wheels and using the same paint jobs. It’s exactly what happened with this 1996 First Editions item I have here.
Metallic Red was the manufacturer’s go-to choice for this casting’s debut, but you could choose from a selection of rims: 5-spoke, 3-spoke, 7-spoke, Saw-blade, and 5-Dot.
I’m a big fan of he Saw-blade look, but the 3-spokes on my Mustang here are just as fun. In recent years I realized how much I want an SN95 in my life, even if I’m afraid it will under perform compared to the ‘90s Japanese cars I’m used to driving.
Photo: autoevolution I’ve unboxed quite a few Mustangs over the past 12 months, and I’ve by no means ticked all the options off the list.
It’s interesting to know that the team in El Segundo tried to turn this casting into a regular Mustang by changing the windshield and painting part of it to resemble a roof.
I don’t think they fooled anyone, but at least Mark Jones went on to create the ‘99 Mustang a few years later. The 1996 Mustang GT lasted all the way up to 2003, when it had one Final Run variation.
That happened two years after its Pavement Pounders appearance, and I’ll show you two cars from that series in a minute.
Ford F-150 Photo: autoevolution I confess I paused what I was doing when I saw the album featuring all these old Hot Wheels , hoping I could get the ones I wanted before anyone else made a move.
Luckily for me, people in my area don’t seem to care about going this far down memory lane. And it’s all quite refreshing when you compare it to the craziness that goes on in the Red Line Club and even other modern Premium series.
While I still haven’t found the Ford F-250 Mark Jones designed about a decade ago, I’m always happy to look at a new F-150.
This one felt familiar, and I soon realized I had previously unboxed its lifted “sibling”, a 2008 Team: Ford Racing iteration with flames on the hood and doors.
Photo: autoevolution While that almost felt like a Monster Truck , this basic version is a depiction of the standard truck. I probably wouldn’t have cared about it 10 years ago, but now that I live in the countryside a lot has changed.
Speaking of which, not only was this part of the 1997 First Editions series, but it also showed up in the Farm Country 5-Pack alongside the Oshkosh Snow Plow, the Tractor, Bronco 4-Wheeler and the Ford Stake Bed Truck.
The Pro Racing iteration that arrived that same year is obviously one of the hottest ones you can go for, and so are the 1998 JC Whitney and the 2003 Highway 35 World Race variations.
You’ll notice I brought my '99 Ford F-150 SVT Lightning out for the photo shoot! It’s always fun to see how the game has changed after 20+ years, isn’t it?
Lamborghini Countach Photo: autoevolution I had already found eight of these cars to purchase and only needed two more for the full story.
The Pavement Pounders set featuring the Future Truck and the Lamborghini Countach felt like the best choice, mainly because I’ve always wanted to see what this old Countach was like.
As far as I know, it was the fifth replica of this machine in Mattel’s portfolio. There was a Sizzlers version in 1978, an Action Racers release in 1987, an LP400 S in 1988 and the Micro Hot Wheels release in 1990.
This 25th Anniversary model is Dave Weise’s creation, and I have first-hand experience with several of his projects including the ‘97 Corvette, the Riley & Scott MK III and the 24/Seven.
Photo: autoevolution He worked on two Lamborghinis during his tenure at Mattel: the Murcielago didn’t arrive until 2003, though. When the Countach debuted in 1997, it featured a Pearl Yellow finish and 5-Dot wheels.
It looked quite a bit more menacing the following year in black! You’d have to chase after nearly 30 variations to have the complete collection, and most of them showed up in toy stores in the 21st century.
Four of them were part of the Pavement Pounders series, where they were paired with three different haulers.
I was honestly a bit disappointing with this model at first, as it’s a bit rough around the edges. But the more I look at it, the happier it makes me for adding it to my shopping list.
Dodge Caravan Photo: autoevolution I somehow ended up with four Dodge collectibles on today’s list, even though I am by no means a fan of the American manufacturer.
The two convertibles are up next, so you could say the Ram truck and the Caravan are here to provide some balance to the unboxing.
I’ve been paying more attention to minivans in the real world in the same way I have been doing with pickup trucks. I don’t mind being a “soccer dad” if it means I can make the kids happy by taking them to practice or a game.
There’s a decent selection of castings in this category including the Ford Aerostar, the Chrysler Pacifica, the Honda Odyssey, and even the Toyota Alphard and the Chevy Astro Van if you must have a metal base and Real Riders wheels.
Photo: autoevolution The Dodge Caravan is the first of two Phil Riehlman-designed models in this story, and I’m delighted to say this is a First Editions model too.
It seems revealing multiple variations of one casting where the wheels are the only differentiating factor was common practice in the late 90s.
I missed out on the Saw-blade wheels again, but you’d probably never see an exotic design like that on a vehicle like this in the real world anyway. At 43 grams, the Caravan is just as heavy as the convertible Mustang and the Porsche 911 GT2 EVO 993 from the Elite 64 series.
Mattel created just over a dozen variations of this Dodge minivan until 2012, when it went out with a bang thanks to the Hot Wheels Boulevard: Big Hits version which had all the defining characteristics of a premium collectible.
Dodge Sidewinder Photo: autoevolution What’s the first thing that comes to mind when you hear the word “Sidewinder”? I though of the rattlesnake, and the air-to-air missile and I must confess I don’t remember ever seeing Dodge’s Dakota Sidewinder concept.
Cadillac Cien’s and Sixteen concepts are the only made-in-America concept cars that somehow left a lasting impression on me back in the day.
I also had no clue about the SEMA Show when this car was revealed there in 1997. But I definitely knew what a Dodge Viper was as I had a photo of one on my old computer’s desktop.
That’s right, this machine had an 8.0-liter Viper V10 engine inside, and it was built on a Riley and Scott chassis but never made it into production.
Photo: autoevolution This First Editions release I have here is a replica of the car shown at SEMA , although I’m unsure where the idea for the purple interior came from.
I struggled to find its good side for the photo session, but it looks way too bulky for me regardless of the angle.
I would have certainly liked to take it for a drive considering the power train, which isn’t something you can enjoy in the 1/64th-scale Universe, though.
Mattel fitted this vehicle with Real Riders wheels in 2004 for the Auto Affinity: Haul 'N' Asphalt series, and you can tell things started going downhill in 2009 when it became an Easter exclusive collectible marking the end of its career.
Ford Mustang Mach 1 Photo: autoevolution As this is the second Mustang today, I risk running out of options soon. I’m just kidding, it would take me years to see all the Mustang variations out there at the rate I’m unboxing and writing about them now.
I can think of at least three other Mustang Mach 1 castings right off the bat: the 2021 model (1:43), Larry Wood’s ‘71 design, and Jun Imai’s old G-Machines Mach 1 which was a 1:50th-scale collectible.
I found three, more modern Mustangs in one of my transport cases for a “family” photo. A keen eye might be able to tell Phil Riehlman’s casting is slightly older, but I think it looks timeless even after 30 years have passed.
It almost didn’t even need two retools along the way. The yellow finish is obviously a big selling point for me. Seeing the rear-window louvers reminds me that someone suggested I take this route with my RX-7 back in 2019.
Photo: autoevolution I already can’t see anything in my side mirrors, why would I compromise the center one as well? Come to think of it, this is the sixth item in the 1998 First Editions series I’ve ever unboxed, and the seventh one is coming right up.
It all feels like a fun little sidequest at this point, and I encourage all of you to find the right “game” for you.
I don’t know what happened in 1999, but Mattel produced five variations of the Mustang Mach 1 with Real Riders wheels, with another one showing up the following year. That Full Grid Exclusive Trailer Edition livery looks similar to the first design on Jun Imai’s '69 Ford Mustang Boss 302 from back in 2012.
The Mach 1 had at least seven other variations you might love to own, and part of me hopes the 2024 Retro Racers 5‑Pack wasn’t the last one we’ll ever see.
Dodge Concept Car Photo: autoevolution I promise this is both the last Dodge and the last Concept Car in today’s story. This one is quite a bit more interesting than the Sidewinder, although it didn’t have a Viper V10 under the bonnet.
Originally called the “Copperhead”, it was meant as a cheaper alternative to the Viper, packing just over 220 bhp from a 2.7-liter V6 engine.
I didn’t have access to a PS console when you could drive one of these in Gran Turismo, and it’s likely not on Mr. Yamauchi’s list of priorities for the near future either.
Phil Riehlman designed the casting for the 1998 First Editions series, and I’m thrilled to report it has a ZAMAC base.
Photo: autoevolution As a result of that, it’s the second heaviest car in today’s story, weighing 54 grams despite it being relatively small overall.
That’s as much as Ryan Tuerck’s FD Toyota GR Corolla or Toretto’s Mazda RX-7 to help you figure out where it stands.
While I realize Copper Fire Orange was the concept car’s original color, I think the 1999 Super Roadsters 4-Car Set variation in black is pretty cool which is rare of me to say.
Real Riders wheels were sadly never an option, and Mattel shelved the project almost a decade and 10 variations since its inception. By 2008, the “Copperhead’ had even switched to a plastic base to make things worse.
Evil Twin Photo: autoevolution I could’ve said that this unboxing focused solely on 20+ years old models if it weren’t for Larry Wood’s Evil Twin.
Sure, it debuted in the 2001 First Editions series with models I’ve already experienced such as La Troca, the Cadillac LMP and the Riley & Scott Mk III. But the variation I have here was part of the 2007 Treasure Hunt series.
That’s when Mattel split the former line in two, creating the regular Treasure Hunt items and the Trea$ure Hunt$ (which you now know as the Super Treasure Hunt).
My car doesn’t have the fancy Spectraflame Red finish and the 6-Spoke Real Riders wheels, and I’m only missing the paintjob here.
Photo: autoevolution Well, “missing” might be an overstatement, as the base color is just as good. It’s far more impressing in the natural light outside the blister card, so give it a chance if you ever find one in the wild.
Evil Twin is one of many castings in the Hot Wheels Universe with two engines up front, and there’s even a Hardnoze take on the concept if you like cartoonish-looking vehicles.
While the latest variation of the casting was available in toy stores back in 2024, you’ll have to travel back 20 years into the past for the rarest of them all.
Only 2,000 units of the 4th Annual Hot Wheels Collectors Nationals Dinner Car were ever made, and it’s almost shocking to see you can get one for less than $50.
Future Truck Photo: autoevolution The usual problem with 2-packs and multipacks in general is that it’s almost impossible to like all of the cars inside.
It’s especially true if we’re not talking about a premium set like Team Transport . In a way, Pavement Pounders feels like Team Transport’s predecessor, although there are many other takes on the concept of packaging a hauler and a fast car in the same box.
You’re looking at an original casting by Fraser Campbell, one that only lasted for two years and seven variations.
The last one was part of Truckin’ Transporters, which predates Racing Rigs. While the truck itself uses six wheels, the trailer brings four more into the equation.
Photo: autoevolution And you’re right in thinking that we’ve never seen these rims on anything else before!
I’m sure my nephews wouldn’t mind the somewhat cartoonish design of the truck, but I can point out a few good points about it all: the detachable trailer and its opening rear door plus the Skate Team livery as I’m still a skateboarder at heart.
Oh and one last thing: it tips the scales at 158 grams, making it the third heaviest Hot Wheels I’ve ever unboxed after the Euro Hauler and the Flipsider Hauler.
That’s it for my October unboxing stories, I’m pretty sure you’ll like the cars I’ll prepare for November.
